findings:
Revision 4 fixes all six problems from the third review, and none of the earlier rounds' findings has come back. The reviewer re-checked the Mine Layer's planning against the real movement limits in its own simulation. A standing player now gets a committed line in about 1.7 s. A player moving at about 100 px/s gets a line laid ahead of them. A cruising player gets the fence line, as the summary now says. Nothing blocking is left, so the plan is approved. Five small refinements, all in the Mine Layer passes task, plus a few doc slips, can be handled by the implementing agent. The most useful one is to state that the layer flies straight at its run-in point rather than turning there gradually. The plan's timing bounds only hold for a straight approach.

### 1. Steering to the run-in point
The plan's own simulation has no turn limit. A layer steering like the Bomber, starting at rest and facing away, first flies the wrong way and loops round. The standing freeze then takes 3.7 s against a 2.5 s bound. The lead-from-ahead row takes 4.7 s against 2.5 s, and the abeam row reaches the 6 s backstop. With a straight seek every row passes.

### 2. No timeout after freezing
The 6 s backstop only counts time before the plan freezes, and the run-in needs the layer within 60 px of its run-in point. Nothing keeps that point away from older mines. If it lands within about 90 px of a live mine, the layer's own avoidance keeps it out indefinitely. This is rare, and impossible against a standing player, but plausible over a long hub session.

### 3. Turning players
In the plan's moving scenario (120 px/s on a 700 px circle), 22 of 144 starting positions reached the 6 s backstop. Between spacing and freezing, the line centre moved a median 165 px, and up to 931 px. The row will probably still pass, because centres on that circle are far apart. Latching the heading until a 30–45° turn cuts the backstops to 12 or 6.

### 4. The 19th mine
The 19th drop is the first mine of the fourth pass, at about 52–60 s even for a standing player. Each backstop in the moving scenario adds 6 s.

### 5. Hysteresis
Every switch between standing and moving re-latches the frame and re-picks the line spot. A player hovering near 60 px/s keeps resetting the target until the backstop.

### 6. Doc slips
These are cosmetic. tasks.json already gives t16 the right sections.
